evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Introduces <Enter>/<Leave> as first-class events for visual feedback without clicks, and defines binding scope (widget vs root), with bind_class/bind_all and add='+'/unbind() flagged as deeper material.

A plain second bind(sequence, callback) on the same widget REPLACES the first handler; add='+' adds another so both fire; unbind(sequence) removes the binding entirely. -- confirmed exactly, all three -- two plain bind() calls give ['second']; then add='+' gives ['second','third']; then unbind() gives [].

A .bind() callback must accept the event argument even when unused, and _event is the conventional name for a deliberately unused parameter. -- confirmed -- omitting the parameter raises TypeError; the _event convention matches PEP 8's underscore guidance and is used consistently in tic_tac_toe.py lines 141-142.

widget.bind() affects only that widget; root.bind() applies at the main window level. -- confirmed -- bindings on a Label do not fire for events on a sibling; root-level bindings are reached via the toplevel entry in the bindtags chain verified in 17.11.

Neither <Enter> nor <Leave> should change game state. -- confirmed against the canonical implementation -- on_cell_enter only calls buttons[i].config(...) and on_cell_leave only calls render(); app.state.board is verifiably unchanged across both.
